subject: history_social
passage: When Marc Isambard Brunel began digging beneath the River Thames in London in 1825, no one had ever built a tunnel under a navigable river. To keep the soft riverbed from collapsing, he used a tunneling shield, an iron frame in which workers excavated the soil in small sections, one at a time. Even so, the river broke through more than once, and the project took eighteen years. When the tunnel finally opened in 1843, it was used only by people on foot, even though Brunel ______ it to carry horse-drawn carriages; the company had run out of money for the long ramps that vehicles would have needed.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: The design work happened before the tunnel opened in 1843, which is itself a past event ("it was used"). An action completed before another past action takes the past perfect, so "had designed" is correct.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The present perfect "has designed" links the action to the present, but the sentence places it before a past event.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The present tense "designs" doesn't fit a design made before a past event in 1843.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The future "will design" places the design after the opening, but the tunnel was already built.
explanation.D: Correct. The past perfect "had designed" shows that the design came before the tunnel opened and was used only by pedestrians.
